International Applicant Requirements
HomeGetting Started International Applicant Requirements
ON THIS PAGE:
Loyola welcomes students from around the world. If you are an international applicant, there are special admission requirements that you may need to complete. Some requirements vary by program, so check the specific conditions for your chosen program when preparing your application. Please consider the following:
Take into account the admissions timeline when choosing your application term.
Submit all application materials early to allow time for admissions decisions and VISA processing.
Note that the VISA process length varies by country.
Be advised! All admissions requirements must be fulfilled before your application can be reviewed for an admission decision.
Quick FAQs for International Applicants
Can the application fee be waived?
We are happy to inform you that Loyola does not charge an application fee!
Can the transcript evaluation be waived?
If you have attended a non-US institution, a transcript evaluation is required and cannot be waived. See details below.
Can I submit my own transcript evaluation?
No. Transcript evaluations must be sent directly to gradapp@luc.edu from a NACES member company before an application will be reviewed for admission. See details below.
Am I required to submit proof of English proficiency?
In most cases, yes. See details below.
I’m an international applicant who received my undergraduate degree outside of the United States, but received (or will have earned prior to admission) my graduate degree from a regionally accredited United States institution. Do I need to submit a transcript evaluation for my undergraduate degree?
No, but transcripts are still required.
Please note that the transcript evaluation will remain on your application checklist until your official graduate transcripts have been received by this office.
If your question isn’t answered above, we are confident it is answered below, so please read carefully for details of requirements for international applicants.
Language Requirements
International applicants whose native language is not English must do the following:
Take a TOEFL*, IELTS, PTE, or Duolingo test. Loyola accepts TOEFL single date and TOEFL MyBest scores.
Score reports should be sent directly from the testing service to gradapp@luc.edu. If an institution code is needed, use Loyola’s code 1412.
Scores are valid for two years from the test date.
Check your program’s specific English language requirements for specific minimum scores.

Transcript Evaluation
Do I need a transcript evaluation?
If you have non-U.S. educational credentials, you will need a transcript evaluation.
What is a transcript evaluation?
A report created by a NACES (National Association of Credential Evaluation Services) member company showing how your non-U.S. degree compares to a U.S. degree.
What must my transcript evaluation show?
For admission to Loyola's graduate or professional programs, the evaluation must show equivalency to at least a U.S. bachelor’s degree. In addition to other suitable equivalencies, the following international qualifications will be considered equivalent to a U.S. bachelor’s degree:
Three-Year Undergraduate Degree from a Signatory Country of the Bologna Declaration:
Applicants with a three-year undergraduate degree from a country that is a signatory to the Bologna Process will be considered to have an equivalent to a U.S. bachelor’s degree. A transcript evaluation is still required for applicants that meet this criteria.
What if I haven’t completed my degree?
The evaluation must confirm that your degree has been awarded; incomplete or in-progress degrees are not accepted.
Should I request a General Evaluation or a Course-by-Course Evaluation?
Check the specific school requirements below.
Can I send a copy of my transcript evaluation report?
No. Only official documents are accepted; copies are not accepted by Loyola.
Can my application be reviewed for admission without the transcript evaluation?
No. The transcript evaluation is needed before your application can be reviewed.
If you have non-U.S. educational credentials, please follow these steps to get a transcript evaluation:
Submit official educational credentials (transcripts, mark sheets, degree certificates, diplomas, etc.) to a NACES (National Association of Credential Evaluation Services) member company.
Request that your evaluation AND the original official transcripts be sent directly to the office of Graduate & Professional Enrollment Management (GPEM) at gradapp@luc.edu (institution code 1412).
Pay the evaluation fee directly to the evaluator.
Loyola Offers 10% SpanTran Discount For Prospective Applicants
SpanTran, a NACES member, offers a custom application for Loyola University Chicago, ensuring you select the right evaluation at a discounted rate. They accept direct document submissions from non-U.S. universities, but also provide a verification service accepting scanned copies of original documents instead of requiring university document submissions.
LEARN MORE
School-Specific Requirements
Some schools have specific transcript or evaluation criteria for their field that you must meet to be considered for admission. Those criteria are:
Applicants for programs in the Quinlan School of Business, Master of Education programs in Elementary Education and Secondary Education, and the Pharmacovigilance Certificate must request a Detailed Report or Course by Course evaluation.
Applicants applying to the Marcella Niehoff School of Nursing may submit an evaluation completed by CGFNS.
Applicants applying to an LLM or MJ program within the School of Law may submit an evaluation completed by LSAC.
Applicants applying to a School of Continuing & Professional Studies undergraduate degree program must submit a catalog match report from Educational Perspectives.
Applicants applying to a School of Continuing & Professional Studies graduate or post-baccalaureate program must submit a report that includes a grade average in addition to the confirmation of degree conferral.
All other applicants should request a General Evaluation with Grade Average.
Current U.S. Travel and Visa Restrictions
Loyola University Chicago welcomes applications from students worldwide and is committed to supporting global education and access. Due to current U.S. travel and visa restrictions, applicants from certain countries are not eligible to receive Form I-20 documentation to apply for F-1 visa. While all complete applications will be reviewed, Loyola is unable to issue immigration documents to individuals from affected countries. Applicants may review the current list of impacted countries provided by NAFSA, noting that the federal government may update this list at any time.
Office of International and Student Scholar Services
The Loyola Office of International and Student Scholar Services (ISSS) provides support and services for international students including comprehensive immigration-related advising services and a diverse array of programming and events to engage international students and scholars with communities on-campus and throughout the city of Chicago.
If you have any questions as an International Applicant, please schedule an appointment with an International Student Advisor.
